column3: BootUI uses owner slots and scopes; sharpit uses endpoint and dependency code objects on the current stack or parent greenlet. Work after endpoint return is outside ownership; eager child task first steps may count as owned.

BootUI checks ownership before value matching; sharpit matches first and walks frames only for a match. Unowned work emits no sink row but its checks consume request budgets and matching rows remain redacted.
BootUI reports command arguments uniformly; sharpit distinguishes argv elements, joined command strings, and explicit executables to avoid naming a program when a matched value belongs to it.
BootUI pushes path values before query values at handler time; sharpit reads scope values at first sink check, path parameters first.
Sharpit uses a per-process keyed blake2b only for emitted rows, non-blocking locks, and generation checks; request end and clear drop references without waiting.
Sharpit manually parses bounded query text, skips malformed value escapes, retains undecodable names by position, and replaces invalid decoded UTF-8.
Sharpit reads exact dict path_params only, accepts exact str/int/float/UUID values, and never invokes application conversion or mapping iteration.
Plan 2 adds the counters and row fields deferred from the journal-only implementation; status retains only output-facing counters. Process and file call sites are not shown in this release.
Secret-looking parameter names are masked at intake and shown as ****** in parameter and detail at every exposure; masked names on one target coalesce.

Process and file rows carry no call site (callSite is null) and file rows report origin unknown: a stack walk per process or file event exceeds the 6 microsecond sensor overhead budget, as measured. Security-sinks rows keep their call site. The budget remains unchanged.
Process and security-sinks rows have null origin; file rows report origin unknown because no stack walk runs on the file event path (see plan2:N2).
Unowned rows carry the hook thread name and the store normalizes it to a thread family for attribution.
Clearing recording clears rings and store with a timestamp; idle and low-footprint suspension retain rows.
Each ringed sensor is teed to its bounded Side Effects ring before journal source filtering; journal source selection does not hide its tab rows.
Coverage wording names command and file path sinks and SHARPIT_AGENT_SECURITY_SINKS_REQUEST_VALUES; SQL and outbound URL sinks are excluded.
The SQL-literal clause is omitted because this release has no SQL sink.
Call-site labels use Python module:qualname rather than Java Class#method.
Holder counters describe requests reaching a sink check; dropped is per sensor ring overflow; notKept stays zero because sharpit has no intern table. Plan 1 D8 is updated accordingly.
Process exit and lifetime fields remain zero or null because the audit hook has no process-exit event.
Rows drain and route resolution occurs on reads from bounded per-sensor rings; a row whose HTTP event was evicted resolves to (unknown route) after the wait.
Attribution is masked per path segment at output; an untemplated request uses the capture-reduced request path.
Startup readiness is the completion of host lifespan startup; without a lifespan rows are not assigned to startup.
The security-sinks catalogue label says request input reaching commands and file paths only.
Origins are limited to application, library, and unknown; Python has no JDK, logging-origin, or class-path categories.
Limitations describe Python interpreter files, absent process-exit data, and route/startup/thread-family attribution instead of JVM files and class loaders.
Secret-looking placeholder names are masked at target output under every exposure, as covered by the secret-shaped path handling.

No journal-clear action is added. clear_recording remains unwired in production until a supported journal clear exists. The Other row text ends with 'Restart the application to see them again.' instead of naming a clear that sharpit does not offer.
